title: Redis data structures
content: Redis is an in-memory data store supporting rich data structures: strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams. Session objects map naturally to hashes, allowing partial field updates without rewriting the whole session blob.

title: Memcached design
content: Memcached is a simple, multithreaded in-memory key-value cache. Values are opaque blobs up to 1MB by default. Its slab allocator and multithreaded architecture give extremely predictable latency under high concurrency.

title: Redis persistence
content: Redis offers optional persistence via RDB snapshots and AOF logs. For session caching this means sessions can survive a restart, at the cost of some write amplification. Memcached has no persistence: a restart empties the cache.

title: Replication and HA
content: Redis supports primary-replica replication, Sentinel failover, and Redis Cluster sharding out of the box. Memcached relies on client-side consistent hashing for distribution and has no built-in replication; losing a node loses its keys.

title: Session TTL semantics
content: Both Redis and Memcached support per-key TTL, which fits session expiry. Redis additionally supports touching TTLs and Lua scripts for atomic check-and-extend patterns used in sliding-window session expiry.

title: Memory efficiency
content: Memcached generally has lower per-key memory overhead for small opaque values due to its slab allocator. Redis costs more memory per key but can offload with hash-field encoding; ziplist/listpack encodings reduce small-hash overhead considerably.

title: Throughput characteristics
content: Memcached scales vertically across many threads on one node and often wins raw GET/SET throughput benchmarks. Redis is mostly single-threaded per shard for command execution (I/O threading exists since 6.0), scaling horizontally via clustering.

title: Healthcare workload constraints
content: Healthcare session data often carries PHI, so encryption in transit (TLS) and at rest, plus auditability, matter. Redis supports TLS natively and ACLs since Redis 6. Memcached supports TLS since 1.5.13 but has coarser authentication (SASL).

title: Operational tooling
content: Redis ships rich introspection: SLOWLOG, MEMORY USAGE, keyspace notifications, and a broad ecosystem (Sentinel, Cluster, RedisInsight). Memcached exposes stats counters and is famously low-maintenance due to its minimal feature surface.

title: Failure modes
content: A cold Memcached restart causes a thundering-herd of session re-creation against the backing store; mitigations include request coalescing. Redis with AOF everysec loses at most one second of session writes on crash, softening cold-start impact.
